key_insight: A nonconforming finite element method solves biharmonic problems on closed smooth surfaces without stabilization or Piola transforms.
engineering_relevance: The approach simplifies finite element implementation for fourth-order surface equations through scalar degrees of freedom and standard assembly.
method: Use reduced enriched quartic elements with vertex values and scalar edge moments.
Assemble elementwise Laplacian inner products on piecewise planar surface triangles.
Establish stability using weak discrete Miranda–Talenti estimates that separate planar vertex residuals from angle defects.
evidence_signal: Analysis proves first-order energy-norm and second-order broken H1- and L2-norm convergence; numerical tests on three surfaces confirm the predicted rates and examine stability constants and angle-defect scaling.
watch_item: Uniform stability is guaranteed on sufficiently refined interpolating meshes of closed smooth surfaces; applicability beyond these assumptions is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: A Finite Element Method for the Surface Biharmonic Problem without Stabilization or Piola Transforms
